findings.summary: first version left a zombie child of the test process (backend could not reap leaders it was refused to signal), tripping the existing p27s zombie assertions later in the same discover run; fixed by pidfd-exact waitid reaping in the test cleanup. Not an implementation defect (a root-owned shell leader cannot occur).

observations: With all pidfd signals refused, PTY hang-up still ends the shell/OMP leaders, so result.verified stays true; the test only asserts no exception and a report.

bash resends SIGHUP to its jobs on hang-up, so EPERM fixtures use nohup'd members; p27t tests type through the UiServer socket when the loop thread runs (direct admit from the test thread races the loop's _flush with a BufferError, a test-threading matter).
